first_row.note: first row has steps==1 in every track (see first_row_steps), consistent with taking the counter as 0 before the first row

reconciliation_sum_window_increments_min.note: windows cover [0, last_full_window_end]; steps in the trailing partial window are excluded from windows, so *_incl_trailing adds them back for the pure arithmetic check

decision.rule: Treat the counter as cumulative with out-of-order delivery of rows inside one reporting batch: cum(T) = running maximum of steps over rows with ms<=T (rows ordered by ms); window increment = cum(T_end) - cum(T_start). Never clip individual diffs; report the window-level net change. Rows at identical ms are kept (no dedup needed: running max is order-independent).
decision.known_limitation: A window boundary falling inside a batch can credit up to the batch's max decrease (<=4 steps) to one window and take it back in the next; the net over the track is exact.
decision.observed_pattern: All decreases lie inside one endDate batch (rows with identical endDate, ms differing by 0-12 ms): rows of a batch are delivered out of order, not counter resets or corrections. Exception in kind: 14_4 has one row with steps==0 inside a batch (-6) and 14_9 a -10 jump inside a batch; both recover within the batch. Sorting by ms (stable) does not fix them, sorting by (endDate, steps) fixes all but 1 event.
decision.metadata_reconciliation_exceptions: 5_7 (metadata totSteps is 1 below the last value) and 14_7 (running max is 1 above the last-row value that equals totSteps); 1 step each
decision.before_first_row: counter taken as 0 before the first row (first row already holds several steps)
